name: Centro Historico
description: The postcard core of Granada, wrapped around Parque Central and the yellow Cathedral. Pastel arcaded streets, grand old houses, cafes, and horse-drawn carriages set the scene, putting the city's landmarks, markets, and everyday services within an easy walk.
bestFor: First-time visitors and nomads wanting walkable colonial charm and convenience

name: Calle La Calzada
tagline: Lively pedestrian street toward the lake
description: Granada's social spine, a pedestrian avenue running from the Cathedral down toward the lakefront. Lined with restaurants, bars, and terraces, it hums with live music and people-watching by night, and offers plenty of dining and traveller energy by day.
bestFor: Sociable nomads who want dining, nightlife, and buzz on the doorstep
pros: Best concentration of restaurants and bars

name: Xalteva and La Merche
description: The western neighbourhoods around La Merced church and Xalteva keep the colonial character while feeling calmer and more residential than the tourist core. Local shops, quieter streets, and a slower rhythm suit longer stays, with the centre still a short walk away.
bestFor: Longer-stay nomads wanting a calmer, more local everyday base
cons: A short walk from the main sights

name: Lakefront and Isletas
description: The eastern edge of Granada meets Lake Nicaragua at the waterfront and port area, the launch point for boat trips into Las Isletas. It trades the colonial streetscape for open water, breezes, and access to the archipelago, though it feels more peripheral.
bestFor: Nature lovers wanting lake access, boat trips, and island day trips
pros: Direct access to the lake and Las Isletas
